round1.verdict: Gap in Setup: it fixes only compactness of K and continuity of f, with no bound or normalization on f. As stated, the Setup cannot support the Main bound sup_K |f| ≤ 1 — e.g. K = {0}, f ≡ 2 satisfies the Setup but violates the claim. A hypothesis such as |f| ≤ 1 on K (or a stated normalization) is missing.
round1.gap: Setup omits the boundedness/normalization hypothesis on f required by the claimed bound; the stated assumptions are satisfied by functions with sup_K |f| arbitrarily large.

round2.gap: The Main bound section asserts sup_K |f| ≤ 1 with no derivation ("The proof is omitted"), so there is no argument to check — only an unsupported claim. The claim is moreover false under the stated Setup: K = {0}, f ≡ 2 is compact-supported, continuous, and satisfies every hypothesis given, yet sup_K |f| = 2. Round 1's gap therefore propagates intact into this section. Two repairs are needed, not one: (i) a substantive hypothesis on f, since merely adding "|f| ≤ 1 on K" would make this section a restatement of its own hypothesis rather than a bound to be proved — a genuine hypothesis (e.g. a normalization sup_K |f| = 1 paired with an a priori estimate, or a Lipschitz/energy condition) plus a proof is required; and (ii) an actual proof of the bound from that hypothesis. Until then, the downstream "sharp for constant functions" remark in the Discussion rests on the same unsupported normalization (sharpness needs an exhibited f with sup_K |f| = 1 under an allowed class, which the current Setup does not define).
